checked_sources: Primary theorem premises: Celani–Nagy–Zuluaga Botero, Bounded distributive lattices with strict implication and weak difference, arXiv:2312.10873v1, Definition 4.3, Theorems 5.7 and 5.10, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.10873
correctness.rationale: The original full two-connective WHB identities and their duality reduce all n-point dual-chain frames to one weakly increasing suffix-threshold sequence 0≤t0≤⋯≤t_(n−1)≤n. Explicit upset calculations reconstruct a→b=top and a←b=bottom for a≤b, otherwise Box b and Diamond a with Diamond the unique left adjoint of monotone top-preserving Box. Counting threshold sequences gives binom(2n,n) named expansions. Each nonempty relation joins all vertices in the initial active rows and final active columns into one component with g=max(0,t0−a) isolates; the empty relation has n components. The fixed-gap summation ∑_{a=1}^{n−g−1}binom(n−g−2,a−1)=2^{n−g−2} yields rank r multiplicity 2^{n−r−1} for 2≤r≤n−1, one at rank n, and binom(2n,n)−2^{n−2} simple for n≥2; n=1 separately has two simple expansions. Our independent direct threshold graph census reproduces n=1..5 rank histograms (2), (5,1), (18,1,1), (66,2,1,1), (244,4,2,1,1). These bounded checks do not prove the all-n duality or formulas; the proof uses the cited general theorems.
residual_risks: Theorem 5.7/5.10 of the external 2023 article are necessary premises; finite enumeration is not a proof of the general duality or Stirling asymptotic.
